question: Use the appropriate for of the verb to complete the sentence. (1)
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2) Mediated**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes how the object of consciousness is not separate but actually **mediated** by consciousness itself. (मध्यस्थ / प्रभावित किया हुआ)
 
• The past participle form **mediated** fits correctly because it shows a condition or state produced by the action of consciousness.
 
• Other forms like **mediating** or **mediates** would disturb the formal and philosophical structure of the sentence.
 
• Thus, the most contextually and grammatically appropriate choice is **mediated**.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2) Mediated**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mediating (मध्यस्थता करते हुए)**: Refers to the present participle/continuous action.

 **Example:** He is mediating between the two groups to resolve the conflict. (Not suitable here)
 
• **Mediates (मध्यस्थता करता है)**: Refers to present tense, singular subject.

 **Example:** A teacher mediates discussions in class. (Not suitable in this abstract philosophical context)
 
• **Has mediated (मध्यस्थता कर चुका है)**: Present perfect tense, indicating completed action.

 **Example:** She has mediated several disputes successfully. (Too specific and temporal for the passage)
